The MEAN columns give the difference between the emulator's and CESM2's pooled means, in \%-points, and Welch's $t$-test on the member means (6--11 emulator members against 6--11 CESM2 members), members being independent realizations. The DISTRIBUTION columns give the ratio of standard deviations, emulator over CESM2, and a two-sample Kolmogorov--Smirnov test on values from which each side's own ensemble-mean trajectory has been removed --- that is, on internal variability with the shared forced trend taken out, which is what makes the samples independent enough to test. ``Same?'' is $p>0.05$.}
